claims.statement: OpenWiki's test suite is run by Vitest, using the vitest runner and @vitest/coverage-v8 as dev dependencies rather than any separate test framework.
Ink terminal-UI components are tested by rendering them with `render` from ink-testing-library and asserting on the rendered frame via `lastFrame()`.
`pnpm test` is a three-stage gate that runs typecheck, then build, then the coverage run in order, so a change must pass type checking and a full build before its coverage test run.
The `typecheck` script type-checks both the server project (tsconfig.json) and the browser/client project (tsconfig.client.json) with `tsc --noEmit`.
The `coverage` script runs `vitest run --coverage`, and `build` compiles both TypeScript projects and copies the visualize client assets.

Coverage uses the V8 provider with `all: true` plus an explicit include of `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`, so files no test imports still appear in the report (as 0%) instead of being omitted from the denominator.

Coverage deliberately excludes files that emit no runtime JS or cannot run in a Node unit test — .d.ts, pure types.ts modules, the telemetry/index.ts barrel, the browser-only visualize/client.ts, and the Ink keyboard state machine setup/credentials/use-init-setup.ts — because their extractable logic lives in separate tested modules.
Coverage reporters are configured as text, text-summary, html, json-summary, and lcov.

Test discovery keeps Vitest defaults and adds one exclusion, `**/benchmarks/*/repo/**`, so an upstream KEB benchmark's reconstructed source tree and its own *.test.ts files are never collected as this project's tests.

The test/ tree mirrors the src/ tree directory-for-directory, so each subsystem's tests live at the path matching its source (e.g. test/agent for src/agent, test/connectors for src/connectors, test/generation for src/generation, test/okf for src/okf, test/integrations for src/integrations).
Tests import source modules directly by relative path (e.g. ../../src/...), so a source module can be unit-tested through Vitest's transform without first building dist/.

The claims tests are split by the claims subsystem's internal boundaries: test/claims/core (resolver-agnostic mutation and error model), test/claims/brains/code (the code claim brain: paths, preflight, runtime, session, store), and test/claims/evidence/repository (repository evidence resource and resolver).

Connector tests keep cross-cutting machinery (config, fetch-with-resilience, MCP client/runtime, tools) at the top level of test/connectors and place each individual source under test/connectors/sources.

Per-source connector tests exercise the source through its ingest() entry point offline: they point $HOME at a throwaway temp dir, feed controlled API responses through a stubbed fetch, and assert on the request built and the normalized raw dump written to disk, with no real network call or OAuth token.

Failure-path tests inject faults with vi.mock plus a vi.hoisted counter that wraps the real module and throws on selected calls while otherwise delegating to the real implementation. test/generation/repository-run.test.ts arms a failureHarness with six counters — manifestReplacements, manifestWrites, metadataWrites, stateWrites, stateRemovals, and sourceMutationsAfterManifestReplacement — that wrap page-manifest.js (recordRepositoryPageCompletion for manifestWrites, replaceRepositoryPageManifest for manifestReplacements plus a mid-replacement source mutation for sourceMutationsAfterManifestReplacement), agent/utils.js (writeLastUpdateMetadata for metadataWrites), and run-state.js (writeRepositoryRunState/removeRepositoryRunState for stateWrites/stateRemovals) to inject manifest-, metadata-, and run-state write/removal failures and prove the runner's recovery and rollback behavior.

Tests that exercise on-disk behavior stay hermetic by creating an OS temp directory with mkdtemp, redirecting $HOME/USERPROFILE or OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR into it, and restoring/cleaning up in afterEach, rather than mocking fs.
Tests that touch Mermaid rendering install jsdom window/document globals by calling ensureDomGlobals() from src/mermaid/dom-shim.ts.

A small number of files named *.e2e.test.ts drive a real vendor SDK path instead of a mock; gemini-enterprise-claude.e2e.test.ts exercises the real Anthropic Vertex SDK and real Mermaid DOM shim using a throwaway offline credentials file so no real token or network request is involved.

The agent subsystem directory holds three OKF-authoring-pipeline test files added in the v0.4.0 cycle: frontmatter-validator.test.ts exercises validateOkfFrontmatter in isolation against accepted/rejected frontmatter families, index-middleware.test.ts drives createOpenWikiIndexMiddleware against a real OpenWikiLocalShellBackend in an mkdtemp dir (including broken-Mermaid failure paths), and wiki-finalizer.test.ts exercises prepareWikiForAuthoring and finalizeWikiArtifacts against an isolated repository-mode backend.

test/okf/frontmatter.test.ts is the broadest OKF frontmatter suite, covering normalizeConceptContent (regenerating frontmatter for bare pages, repairing optional fields while preserving producer-defined extensions, stamping a localized concept type) and the parseFrontmatterFields/renderFrontmatter/validateOkfFrontmatter/repairOkfFrontmatter/validatePersistedFile helpers, mirroring src/okf/frontmatter.ts.

test/generation/repository-run.test.ts is the end-to-end integration test for the repository generation workflow: it imports parseFrontmatterFields and validateOkfFrontmatter from src/okf/frontmatter.ts and the beginRepositoryRun/submitRepositoryPlan/nextRepositoryPage/submitRepositoryPage/finishRepositoryRun lifecycle plus the captureRepositoryPageSnapshot/skipRepositoryPage/inspectRepositoryPageClaims skip-and-inspect primitives from src/generation/repository-run.ts, and drives the full begin→submit_plan→next_page→submit_page→finish lifecycle (and the skip/restore path) against a temporary committed Git repository, arming the failure harness in beforeEach and removing temp directories in afterEach.

In the repository-run test, finishRepositoryRun accepts a skippedPageSnapshots list so finishing after a skip leaves the original page Markdown and Claims in place, removes the run-state file, and stamps an interrupted last-update status; the 'resets an interrupted skipped job to pending on resume' test then proves resuming such a run re-queues the skipped page as pending rather than carrying the skipped status forward.

test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts drives runNativeRepositoryGeneration through a deepagents/repository-run.js mock harness whose vi.hoisted counter set arms planner and page-worker failure modes (pageWorkerFailures, pageWorkerPostSubmitFailures, workerExitsWithoutSubmit, duplicatePlanSubmission, invalidPlanSubmissions, invalidPageSubmissions, driftOnce, noop); the 'restores and leaves a page pending when its worker does not submit' test sets workerExitsWithoutSubmit so a page worker exits without calling submit_page, the runner invokes captureRepositoryPageSnapshot/skipRepositoryPage (counted by restoreCalls) to restore the snapshot, marks that page skipped, finishes the run, and emits a text event telling the user the page will be reconsidered on the next update.

test/visualize/page.test.ts pins the exact CDN script versions the visualizer loads (force-graph, marked, dompurify, mermaid) and requires each script tag to carry an SRI integrity plus crossorigin=anonymous attribute, so a version bump is forced through this test with a fresh hash review; it also guards the issue #670 overlay-layout regression that the hint and legend live inside #graph with a height-capped, scrollable legend, and a CSP Google Fonts regression test asserts the page's Content Security Policy allows the origins the page itself requests (style-src allows fonts.googleapis.com, the stylesheet the <link> tag loads, and font-src allows fonts.gstatic.com, the font files that stylesheet references).

test/visualize/client-interaction.test.ts runs under @vitest-environment jsdom to test the browser-only src/visualize/client.ts: it mounts a minimal DOM, replaces the ForceGraph/marked/DOMPurify/mermaid/ResizeObserver/fetch globals with recording stubs, imports the client under data-static-export, and asserts the issue #670 regression that background clicks are not wired to any handler (so clicking blank graph space never clears the reader) while node clicks select a page and highlight its sidebar entry. It also asserts the graph-label decluttering feature driven by shouldShowNodeLabel: no labels are painted by default, hovering a node draws only that node's label, and clicking a node draws its label plus the labels of its directly connected neighbours, by calling the registered onNodeHover/onNodeClick handlers and painting every node through the recorded nodeCanvasObject handler to collect the fillText calls.

test/agent/update-noop.test.ts is the dedicated suite for the update no-op fast-skip path: it builds a real committed Git repository with an OpenWiki tree and exercises getUpdateNoopStatus across the conditions that should and should not skip (unchanged HEAD, output-language change, equivalent primary-language request, committed-only dirty run metadata, page-manifest migration, uncommitted worktree changes, ignored-only paths, OpenWiki-only commits). It also guards the metadata-refresh path so a skip preserves the persisted language (mirroring runOpenWikiAgent's writeLastUpdateMetadata refresh) and covers shouldCheckUpdateNoop's gating conditions.

test/agent/repository-source-fingerprint.test.ts exercises createRepositorySourceFingerprint/createRepositorySourceSnapshot and getRepositoryChangedPaths against a committed Git repository in mkdtemp: it pins fingerprint stability and sensitivity (tracked/staged/unstaged content, deletions, untracked files, executable-bit, symlink-target changes, .openwikiignore rules), the exclusion of generated pages/Claims sidecars/run metadata, and failure-mode races injected by wrapping node:fs/promises with vi.mock — a TOCTOU race where an inspected file becomes a symlink before opening (the fingerprinter fails closed rather than following the swapped target), plus Windows stat-identity drift tests. On non-Windows the same-file guard keys on dev/ino; on Windows it falls back to size/mtimeNs/birthtimeNs and excludes ctimeNs (which can change for the same file between lstat and FileHandle.stat). The tests stub process.platform to win32 and inject stat mutations via the mocked open: a dev/ino drift and a ctimeNs-only drift both still resolve, while a size/mtimeNs/birthtimeNs change rejects with 'Source path changed while fingerprinting'.

test/generation/page-manifest.test.ts covers the page-manifest persistence and completion surface (readRepositoryPageManifest, writeRepositoryPageManifest, replaceRepositoryPageManifest, recordRepositoryPageCompletion, seedRepositoryPageManifest, isRepositoryPageCompletionCurrent, atomic-rename replacement): it injects a manifest-rename failure by wrapping node:fs/promises with vi.mock and asserts the manifest is not left in a half-written state, refuses to advance an unverified or mismatched Claims page, and records the exact verified page bytes and source checkpoint on success.

test/generation/run-state.test.ts covers writeRepositoryRunState/readRepositoryRunState/removeRepositoryRunState against a temp root: the atomic write/read, validation rejection (a wrong schemaVersion must not replace durable state), and temp-file cleanup when rename fails.

test/generation/page-jobs.test.ts exercises createRepositoryPlan and reconcilePageClaims through a ClaimSession with a deterministic evidence resolver. The createRepositoryPlan suite pins plan construction (init requires quickstart, forbids init deletions and quickstart deletion, rejects duplicate pages and generate/delete overlap, rejects structural/reserved working pages, normalizes inputs and orders quickstart last). The reconcilePageClaims suite pins sparse reconciliation: omitted issue-free Claims are retained without round-tripping, a stale or unresolved Claim requires an explicit confirm/update/retract decision, duplicate sparse proposals and conflicting double-decisions are rejected, retracting every Claim on a factual page is forbidden, an already-absent retraction is an idempotent retry, Claim fingerprints with delimiter characters are not conflated, and session state stays atomic when evidence resolution fails.

test/ingestion/code-mode.test.ts exercises ensureCodeModeRepoSetup and runCodeModeConnectors against temp repositories: it parses the generated GitHub Actions workflow YAML, pins the agent files and workflow/provider blocks (including ordered steps, the failure-propagation propagate step, and the PR annotation), and asserts the OpenWiki <!-- OPENWIKI:START -->/<!-- OPENWIKI:END --> snippet contract.

test/integrations/protocol.test.ts exercises the strict Zod schemas in src/integrations/core/protocol.ts: BeginInput (strict, trims root/language, rejects unknown modes and extra fields), RunInput/NextPageInput (shared strict UUID run identity), SubmitPlanInput (strict, rejects extra fields), PlanPageInput (canonicalizes path/title/purpose/seedPaths/relatedPages/instructions), and SubmitPageInput (the sparse Claim reconciliation schema with confirmedClaimIds/claims/retractedClaimIds). It rejects a proposed Claim with empty evidence and one carrying a code-owned version (only bare resource is accepted), and pins isValidHostId's bounded canonical identity rules ([a-z0-9-]{1,64}, rejecting uppercase, underscore, and over-length).

test/integrations/session-manager.test.ts exercises HostSessionManager.create and its single-run adapter over the real repository lifecycle. It asserts the ordered ten-tool surface (the four retrieval tools plus openwiki_begin → openwiki_submit_plan → openwiki_next_page → openwiki_inspect_page_claims → openwiki_submit_page → openwiki_finish) and that inspectPageClaims is exposed on demand. It covers resumability across different hosts (a codex-started run resumed by claude-code), nested-path-to-Git-root resolution via realpath, the strict active-run-id guard, begin conflict mapping (a conflicting mode rejects with conflict and retains the prior active run), the one-operation-at-a-time guard, repository lifecycle failure mapping to bounded HostIntegrationErrors, retention of active state when finish fails, the durable-finish completion that clears active state, and an older process-local run being cleared after a proven update no-op.

test/integrations/mcp-server.test.ts exercises createOpenWikiMcpServer through linked in-memory MCP transports. It asserts the server advertises the full ordered tool surface — the four retrieval tools (openwiki_list_workspaces, openwiki_list_wikis, openwiki_search, openwiki_read) followed by the six lifecycle tools (openwiki_begin/openwiki_submit_plan/openwiki_next_page/openwiki_inspect_page_claims/openwiki_submit_page/openwiki_finish) — and that the INSTRUCTIONS embedding (from src/integrations/mcp/server.ts) leads with retrieval/search guidance (do not enumerate or preload wikis at task start, search only when grounded, the workspace_required / openwiki_list_workspaces / openwiki_list_wikis / openwiki_read flow, and treating wiki content as context) before the sparse-workflow generation guidance — author with the host's native repository tools, openwiki_submit_plan/openwiki_next_page/openwiki_inspect_page_claims/openwiki_submit_page, that issue-free Claims are retained automatically and only sparse Claim decisions are submitted, the stale or unresolved recheck requirement, Never report success before finish, and source drift invalidated the plan — while never mentioning the removed openwiki_resolve_claims. It also covers successful tool calls (text JSON plus structured content) and error bounding: a HostIntegrationError is surfaced as a bounded isError result while an unknown failure is replaced with a generic OpenWiki MCP operation failed. message that never leaks the sensitive text to the client or stderr. A lifecycle smoke test completes one factual init page through all six transport calls and verifies the Claim was persisted via ClaimsStore.

test/git-repo-connector.test.ts builds real throwaway git repos in temp dirs and drives the git-repo connector across two runs: it asserts the second-run manifest describes what was committed since the recorded head (issue #409), naming the file added in the new commit rather than the already-ingested first commit and carrying the prior head as previousHead, and that a first run reports the working-tree diff only with no previousHead, while a second run against an unreachable recorded head (as after a force-push or garbage-collected rewrite) falls back to the working-tree diff rather than throwing.

test/ingest-all-connectors.test.ts pins the openwiki_ingest_all_connectors failure-isolation contract (issue #412): it mocks the connector registry with two fake connectors — one that resolves and one that rejects — and asserts the tool still returns both outcomes, so a throwing connector does not discard a succeeding connector's result; the failure is surfaced as an error status with the message mirrored into warnings while the success keeps its rawFiles.

test/x-connector-stream-isolation.test.ts pins X-connector per-stream failure isolation (issue #412): stubbing fetch so one stream (mentions) returns 429 while another (user_posts) succeeds, it asserts the run does not abort — the succeeding dump is kept, the failing stream's failure is surfaced as a warning, both streams were still attempted, and state is still written; a complementary case where every stream fails asserts an error status (not a benign skip) with the per-stream warning.

test/openrouter-debug-fetch.test.ts pins the OpenRouter debug-fetch concurrency contract (issue #411): ChatOpenRouter calls globalThis.fetch directly, so installOpenRouterDebugFetch patches the global. The test asserts that a single run restores the exact original fetch on detach, that overlapping runs each keep their own captured failure and the real fetch is restored exactly once — only after the last run detaches, reference-counted so a redundant restore() is a no-op that does not prematurely restore while another run is active — that an OpenRouter failure fans out to every active run's sink while each run can clear its own failure, and that non-OpenRouter requests pass through untouched. It also pins the transient-404 retry contract (only a provider 404 carrying error.metadata.provider_name is retried, not an ordinary 404, and a non-cloneable request body is never resent) and the malformed-success classification: a 200 body that is invalid JSON, missing choices, or has a non-object first choice/message is converted to a retryable 502 OpenRouterError (surfaced through both the raw fetch response and ChatOpenRouter.invoke), while a transient provider 404 preceding such a malformed success is retried first before the malformed response is classified.

test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts covers two additional repository-runner failure semantics. 'continues when the planner repeats the same accepted plan' (armed via duplicatePlanSubmission) repeats the accepted submit_plan call and asserts the runner proceeds to page generation rather than treating the repeat as a conflict (planSubmissionCalls=2 with a duplicatePlanToolResults entry, the page still completes). 'keeps a durably completed page after a later worker failure' (armed via pageWorkerPostSubmitFailures) makes the page worker throw after submit_page succeeds and asserts the page is not rolled back — restoreCalls stays 0 and the page remains complete — because runPageAgent guards its streamWorkerTools catch with `if (submitted) return { status: "submitted" };` so a post-submit worker throw returns a submitted outcome rather than calling skipRepositoryPage.

test/agent/stream-redaction.test.ts pins parseAgentStreamChunk's suppression of file, image, input_file, and image_url content blocks that carry base64 blobs (which must never reach the terminal) while allowing adjacent text blocks in the same chunk to stream through normally; it also covers plain-text streaming, nested task (subgraph) output, model_request namespace classification (a top-level model_request:* namespace is tagged main while a task + model_request:* namespace is tagged subgraph), tool lifecycle normalization (on_tool_start/on_tool_end/on_tool_error), the updates-mode state-diff extraction default for openai-compatible providers (tagged main or subgraph by namespace), tool-call-only messages in updates chunks returning null (a message carrying only tool_calls has no renderable text), and rejection of malformed stream chunks.

test/cli/diagnostics/error-diagnostics.test.ts exercises getErrorDiagnostics, the helper behind the --debug diagnostic surface: a plain Error returns nothing with debug off, debug mode extracts name, message, and an inline HTTP status parsed from the message; the stack is included only when OPENWIKI_DEBUG is set and is then sanitized (secret-like patterns such as a bearer sk-or-v1-... token are replaced with a [REDACTED:OPENROUTER_API_KEY] placeholder) and truncated to exactly 2000 characters with a trailing '...'; it also covers HTTP status and case-insensitive header extraction, OpenRouter metadata extraction (metadata.provider_name) that happens even with debug off, redaction of secret-like keys inside stringified metadata, previous_errors capping at five with a metadata.previous_errors.more note for the remainder, nested response fields surfaced under a dotted prefix, and — in debug mode only — rootCause extraction that walks the cause chain to its innermost non-cyclic cause (rootCause.message/rootCause.code), redacts secret-like patterns in the root-cause message, and stops on a cause cycle.

test/config/env.test.ts exercises parseEnv/formatEnv: parseEnv does atomic single-pass unescaping of backslash escapes in double-quoted values, including carriage return (\r) handling and the Windows-path corruption regression where a raw backslash escaped to \\ immediately before a path segment starting with n or r (e.g. C:\name\creds.json) must not be misread as the \n/\r escape sequence on parse; the parseEnv <-> formatEnv round-trip suite confirms values, carriage returns, and the Windows path regression survive a format -> parse round-trip.

test/connectors/mcp-client.test.ts buildChildEnv suite now pins the mcp-empty-env-var fix: a declared env var set to an empty string (MCP_EMPTY set to "") is treated as present and resolves to "", not as missing, so empty-string env vars survive the child-environment boundary rather than being dropped.

test/ingestion/code-mode.test.ts pins CLAUDE.md handling in ensureCodeModeRepoSetup: when neither agent file exists only AGENTS.md is created — CLAUDE.md is deliberately not created, because Claude Code reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists and creating one would only shadow it; when CLAUDE.md already exists but AGENTS.md does not, setup creates AGENTS.md and rewrites CLAUDE.md as a simple @AGENTS.md reference rather than a copy of AGENTS.md's content (it contains @AGENTS.md, not an inert Markdown link, and is shorter than AGENTS.md); when CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md it inlines the instructions instead of emitting an @AGENTS.md import that would point the file at itself (resolvesToSameFile); and a pre-existing CLAUDE.md that only imports AGENTS.md (e.g. @AGENTS.md) is preserved unchanged rather than overwritten, so an import-only CLAUDE.md survives a re-setup.

The evals/ledger (LEDGER) and evals/deepswe (DeepSWE) evaluation harnesses under evals/ are self-contained subsystems outside the application test/ tree and the pnpm test gate, with their own entry points, type config, and test runners, so changing an eval harness does not require the application test gate and vice versa.

LEDGER ships its own TypeScript project: evals/ledger/tsconfig.json extends the root tsconfig.json, sets noEmit and declaration:false, and widens include to **/*.ts so it type-checks eval source that sits outside the application src/ root.

LEDGER's harness is wrapped by the npm scripts eval:ledger (runs `tsx evals/ledger/run.ts`, the live checkpoint-replay evaluation) and eval:ledger:typecheck (runs `tsc --noEmit -p evals/ledger/tsconfig.json`), plus eval:ledger:reevaluate which re-judges a completed run without re-invoking OpenWiki; these are separate from the application typecheck/test scripts.

LEDGER's test suite is Vitest, but the evals/ledger/**/*.test.ts files are not driven by the root vitest.config.ts (which only tunes discovery and src/ coverage); they run as ordinary Vitest tests invoked explicitly via `pnpm exec vitest run evals/ledger`, and the normal suite is offline with deterministic evaluator/system implementations (live calibration opt-in via LEDGER_LIVE=1).

DeepSWE is a Python harness with no TypeScript/Vitest footprint: its tests are Python unittest modules under evals/deepswe/tests/ (test_run.py, test_analyze_openwiki_usage.py) run via `python -m unittest discover -s evals/deepswe/tests -p 'test_*.py'` inside the pinned Harbor/LiteLLM environment, and the harness itself is driven by `python3 evals/deepswe/run.py` with no npm script defined for it in package.json.

test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts covers coerceRepositoryWorkerModelResponse, the normalization the repository-worker NO_DELEGATION_MIDDLEWARE applies before LangChain validates each wrapModelCall response. OpenAI-compatible providers can emit a first SSE delta without role:"assistant" (e.g. a reasoning-only first delta), so the aggregated message arrives as a generic ChatMessage/ChatMessageChunk instead of an AIMessage/AIMessageChunk, which LangChain would reject. 'coerces roleless generic streaming aggregates before LangChain validates wrapModelCall' feeds a role-undefined ChatMessageChunk carrying additional_kwargs.reasoning_content and raw tool_calls and asserts the result is an AIMessageChunk preserving the text, reasoning_content, and collapsed tool_calls (type:"tool_call"); 'coerces generic assistant messages before LangChain validates wrapModelCall' feeds an explicit-role assistant ChatMessage and asserts it becomes an AIMessage with parsed tool_calls; 'leaves non-assistant generic model responses untouched' asserts a user-role ChatMessageChunk is returned unchanged so non-assistant output is never silently rewritten. The same 'filters DeepAgents automatic task capability at the model boundary' test pins the middleware's removal of the general-purpose task tool from the model-facing request.

test/agent/repository-prompts.test.ts exercises the repository planner and page-worker prompt builders (createRepositoryPlannerPrompt/createRepositoryPagePrompt from src/agent/repository-prompts.ts) against fully-shaped ActiveBeginView/RepositoryPageWorkerJob fixtures. It pins that the planner prompt carries the actual user/connector context, the per-page committed update windows (with 'Baseline <head>' or 'Baseline unknown (full review required)'), the claim issues requiring reconciliation, the wiki goal, and the planning instructions (hierarchical paths, relatedPages, submit_plan directly), and that the page-worker prompt propagates only the Claims requiring explicit reconciliation, stamps the 'You own exactly <path>' ownership line, and emits the sparse-Claim and canonical-evidence (repo://...) guidance.

test/agent/vertex-surface.test.ts exercises the Vertex AI surface dispatch in src/agent/vertex-surface.ts. resolveVertexSurface routes Claude ids to the anthropic surface, partner/MaaS ids (meta, mistral, deepseek, qwen, codellama) to the openai-maas surface, and xAI Grok ids (xai/grok-..., bare grok-..., publishers/xai/models/grok-...) to the openai-maas surface — Grok is served over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint like every other partner model, and falling through to gemini would address it as a non-existent publishers/google/models/grok-... path. Gemini/Gemma ids and unknown publishers default to gemini, and the family-token boundary (^|/) prevents a token embedded mid-word (e.g. gemini-metallica) from being misclassified. The suite also pins stripPublisherPath/toVertexPublisherModel, the regional vs. global vertexOpenAIBaseUrl endpoint construction, withAnthropicAuthEnvNeutralized (hides ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN during construction and restores the prior value — or prior absence — even if construction throws), and createVertexAuthFetch (injects a fresh bearer token per request and throws before the request when no access token is available).

test/config/env.test.ts pins the MANAGED_ENV_KEYS membership: the output-token limits (OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, OPENWIKI_BEDROCK_MAX_TOKENS), the stream idle timeout (OPENWIKI_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT), the repository page-worker concurrency (OPENWIKI_PAGE_CONCURRENCY), the gemini-enterprise (Vertex) Google Cloud settings (GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT/GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION/GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS), the AI-Studio GEMINI_API_KEY, the hosted OpenAI-compatible provider base URLs (BASETEN_BASE_URL, BOB_BASE_URL, FIREWORKS_BASE_URL, NVIDIA_BASE_URL), the reasoning-effort settings (OPENWIKI_REASONING_EFFORT, OPENWIKI_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_REASONING_EFFORT_SUPPORTED), and the OpenAI-compatible Entra authentication mode and scope (OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_AUTH immediately followed by OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_ENTRA_SCOPE in provider order). test/config/constants.test.ts pins resolveProviderBaseUrl defaults and overrides for the hosted OpenAI-compatible providers, where BOB_BASE_URL (via BOB_BASE_URL_ENV_KEY) and the baseten/fireworks/nvidia keys override the built-in defaults while a whitespace-only override falls back to the default, plus resolvePageConcurrency (defaults to DEFAULT_PAGE_CONCURRENCY===1, accepts trimmed integers up to MAX_PAGE_CONCURRENCY, rejects out-of-range/non-integer) and resolveProviderRetryAttempts (raises its default to PARALLEL_PROVIDER_RETRY_ATTEMPTS for pageConcurrency>1 unless overridden), alongside model-id validation, provider normalization/resolution, per-provider max-output-token ceilings, stream-idle-timeout resolution, reasoning capability flags, base-URL validation (rejecting /chat/completions endpoints for openai-compatible), and the Bedrock AWS-SDK credential/region surface.

runNativeRepositoryGeneration documents pages through a PageWorkerPool of up to pageConcurrency slots (runPendingPageAgents/runWorkerLoop in src/agent/repository-runner.ts): with more than one worker, quickstart is held back from the first wave and documented last in a single-worker pass; concurrent generating progress events carry completedCount and the inFlightPages list while a single worker keeps the historical event shape; a worker that fails with a 429 is skipped and the pool size is lowered by one with a 'Reduced page concurrency' text event, while an ordinary worker failure is skipped without lowering concurrency; a fatal submitRepositoryPage error stops new jobs, lets in-flight workers settle, and is rethrown before finish so the run never finalizes with a pending page. test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts pins these contracts with pageConcurrency passed through runHarness and the holdPageWorkers/holdNextPageAcquisition gates.

test/cli/run-log/ tests the pure helpers that reduce the OpenWikiRunEvent stream into the items the Ink App renders, each in isolation: reducer.test.ts exercises appendRunLogEvent (text concatenation, subgraph-narration dropping, repository_progress stage replacement that retains concurrent-worker completedCount/inFlightPages, tool grouping that stays running until every call ends, and bounded unique path-activity tracking for reads/writes/tasks); progress.test.ts pins formatRepositoryProgress/formatRepositoryPrintProgress (single-worker page line vs. multi-worker 'N of M · K in flight' line); summary.test.ts pins formatRunCompletionTitle and formatCompletedRunCounts; activity.test.ts pins getToolPathActivities path normalization/scope classification, isOpenWikiPagePath, and the activity/exploration tree renderers; tool-input.test.ts pins parseToolInput and countToolTargets.

test/integrations/installer.test.ts is the broad host-installer suite for src/integrations/install/installer.ts. It pins the host integration registry: the nine supported targets (bob, codex, claude, opencode, cursor, kiro, omp, antigravity, copilot) with their producerActor identities, per-scope skill directories and MCP-config files, getHostTarget resolution, and that bob shares codex's .agents/skills/openwiki directory while every other host's user skill directory is distinct. It exercises HostIntegrationInstaller install/uninstall/status across every target, asserting a project install from a subdirectory writes at the Git root (not the subdirectory) and rejects installation outside a Git repository, that user and project installations are independent (uninstalling one leaves the other intact), that a modified receipt (whitespace-only MCP command, removed skill, or removed MCP entry) reports modified, that uninstalling a modified integration rejects with conflict leaving files in place, that host directory cleanup preserves the host root derived from the skill path, and that resolveCanonicalSkillBundle resolves the same on-disk integrations/openwiki bundle from both source (installer.ts) and built (installer.js) layouts.

test/integrations/config-adapters.test.ts exercises the per-format MCP-config adapters in src/integrations/install. The atomic-write suite pins that writeTextAtomic preserves file mode bits and leaves no temporary sibling. The JSON, Codex TOML, and OpenCode JSONC ownership suites each pin create/preserve/recognize/remove of the exact OpenWiki entry, that property order is irrelevant but shape drift (a non-matching command) rejects with conflict without changing bytes, that malformed config rejects with invalid_input leaving bytes unchanged (reported as modified), and that a recognized prior entry is replaced while an unrecognized one is left alone. It also round-trips host-specific layouts like Cursor's .cursor/mcp.json.

test/visualize/visualize-graph.test.ts exercises buildGraph/splitFrontmatter/firstHeading from src/visualize/graph.ts against throwaway temp wikis. It pins frontmatter parsing (scalars, quoted titles, inline and dashed lists, and the no-frontmatter passthrough), the first-H1 heading lookup, and the graph builder: nodes exclude INSTRUCTIONS.md scaffolding, the root index.md is titled Home, directed edges resolve links both ways and record backlinks on the target, links to missing pages and self-links are dropped, Unicode and special-character link targets are decoded (with malformed URL escapes not blocking valid links and a raw % preserved in filenames), encoded and Unicode links are deduplicated, and a symlink that escapes the wiki root is not followed.

The repository runner groups every worker of one run into a single LangSmith thread: streamWorkerTools passes resolveTraceThreadId(run.state.runId) as configurable.thread_id to both the planner's and each page worker's agent.stream call, so LangSmith (which groups by configurable.thread_id copied into run metadata) collapses the planner and per-page workers into one thread. The thread id is safe to share across concurrent workers only because they have no checkpointer.

resolveTraceThreadId in src/config/constants.ts returns the trimmed OPENWIKI_TRACE_THREAD_ID env override when it is set and non-empty, otherwise the durable runId, so CI can name a run's LangSmith thread after the change that caused the run while local runs default to the run id.

test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts pins LangSmith thread grouping in a 'LangSmith thread grouping' describe block. The harness mocks createDeepAgent to wrap the returned agent's stream method, pushing each stream(input, config) invocation's config onto harness.streamConfigs. 'tags the planner and every concurrent page worker with the run's thread id' runs with pageConcurrency: 2 and asserts streamConfigs has length 1 + planPaths.length (one planner plus one worker per planned page) and that every config.configurable equals { thread_id: HARNESS_RUN_ID }. 'uses OPENWIKI_TRACE_THREAD_ID when CI sets it' stubs the env with a padded override (' ingest-3280b3e ') and asserts the trimmed value ('ingest-3280b3e') is used for every worker's thread_id.

test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts pins LangSmith trace names in a 'LangSmith trace names' describe block: the first captured agentOptions.name equals PLANNER_AGENT_NAME ('planning agent'), and the remaining worker names sorted equal planPaths.map(workerAgentName) sorted. It also asserts workerAgentName directly, including the nested-path case workerAgentName('/openwiki/coverage/forms/ho-3.md') -> 'worker agent: coverage/forms/ho-3', which strips the /openwiki/ prefix and .md suffix so a run's thread reads as one planner plus one worker per page. PLANNER_AGENT_NAME and workerAgentName are exported from src/agent/repository-runner.ts, where the planner agent is built with name: PLANNER_AGENT_NAME and each page worker with name: workerAgentName(job.path).

The narrowest vitest command for the repository-runner LangSmith thread/trace tests is `pnpm exec vitest run test/agent/repository-runner.test.ts`, scoped by test name with -t 'tags the planner and every concurrent page worker with the run's thread id' (shared thread_id), -t 'uses OPENWIKI_TRACE_THREAD_ID when CI sets it' (trimmed env override), or -t 'names the planner and each page worker after its page' (PLANNER_AGENT_NAME and workerAgentName).

test/agent/create-model.test.ts constructs LangChain chat models (no network call — auth/clients resolve lazily) to pin the gemini-enterprise (Vertex) surface dispatch (Claude→ChatAnthropic, MaaS→ChatOpenAI, Gemini/Gemma→ChatGoogle, publisher-path stripping, the explicit max-output-token limit across all Vertex surfaces, the global endpoint when location is unset, and the missing-project guard), the gemini (AI Studio) surface, the Anthropic output-token ceiling, the OpenAI-compatible transport selection (Chat Completions vs. Responses, redundant content-array normalization, streaming opt-in), the provider-neutral maxTokens mapping, the reasoning configuration, and the OpenRouter output-token cap. Its companion test/agent/create-model-entra.test.ts pins the OpenAI-compatible Entra ID authentication wiring in createModel: default and explicit api-key modes preserve the static key, while entra-id mode passes a renewable callback (not the static key) as apiKey/clientConfig.apiKey honoring the Responses-API and streaming opt-ins and binding clientConfig.baseURL; it rejects a non-HTTPS OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL before model construction and rejects an invalid OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_AUTH mode.

test/agent/entra-auth.test.ts is the dedicated suite for createEntraTokenProvider in src/agent/entra-auth.ts, mocking @azure/identity (DefaultAzureCredential, WorkloadIdentityCredential) via vi.hoisted. It pins lazy one-time Azure Identity construction with concurrent first-request coalescing (a single getToken for parallel callers), workload-identity preference when AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE/AZURE_CLIENT_ID/AZURE_TENANT_ID are set (refreshing past expiry without reconstructing the provider, never falling back to DefaultAzureCredential on workload failure), cached-token reuse while valid, expiry-driven refresh, failure recovery (a failed acquisition is retried and the SDK error is wrapped as 'Unable to obtain a Microsoft Entra ID access token.' without leaking the private cause), and a parameterized endpoint-safety guard rejecting non-HTTPS, credentials-in-URL, and cloud-metadata endpoints before credentials are acquired. A second describe block drives a real model invocation through a stubbed gateway fetch to prove token refresh across the chat/responses × JSON/SSE matrix: two requests past the token lifetime use two distinct bearer tokens, the request URL/stream body match the selected surface/transport, and a token-acquisition failure never reaches the gateway.

test/agent/environment-debug-value.test.ts pins formatEnvironmentDebugValue, the helper behind the --debug env dump that can end up in pasted bug reports: it classifies the Entra auth mode and scope as non-secret configuration (printed verbatim), echoes model/provider selectors verbatim, reports an unset variable as 'unset', previews unknown short values by length only and long values by head/tail, and scrubs URL values (stripping credentials, query, and fragment with a 'redacted=auth+query+hash' marker, degrading to a length preview when the value is not a parseable URL).

test/setup/credentials/init-setup-entra.test.tsx renders the InitSetup wizard with walkAllSteps and mocks getSavedEnvValue to walk the OpenAI-compatible Entra path (provider → Entra ID auth → base URL → scope) without ever prompting for an API key: the base-URL step seeds the saved OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL and the scope step shows OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_ENTRA_SCOPE, so the Entra flow never requests a static key.

test/config/env-behavior.test.ts is the runtime-behavior counterpart to the pure parseEnv/formatEnv suite: it resets the module registry and mocks os.homedir() before dynamically importing src/config/env.ts so every test binds ~/.openwiki/.env to a throwaway temp directory (the path is computed at module load). It pins loadOpenWikiEnv (a saved managed key loads into process.env but never overwrites a key already present, and OPENAI_BASE_URL is loaded while OPENAI_ORG_ID/OPENAI_PROJECT remain deprecated and dropped), saveOpenWikiEnv (owner-only file permissions, deprecated-key stripping, in-process seeding, dropping empty values rather than persisting KEY='', an ENOSPC atomic-swap failure that leaves the original file intact, and serialized overlapping saves that preserve disjoint updates), the shell/file snapshot helpers (getShellEnvValue/getSavedEnvValue), and getCredentialDiagnostics — which surfaces the Entra auth mode and scope, each provider credential key, and the hosted OpenAI-compatible base URLs; masks secrets by length while echoing base URLs verbatim; validates the model id, provider, output-token limits, Bedrock max tokens, stream-idle timeout (zero disables the watchdog with a warning only for the active Bedrock provider), the /chat/completions base-URL warning, the Bob base-URL warning, and the OpenAI-compatible Responses-API/streaming/reasoning-effort boolean opt-ins; and reports the source precedence of process.env over ~/.openwiki/.env.

test/config/constants.test.ts OpenAI-compatible authentication configuration block pins the Entra surface: resolveOpenAICompatibleAuthMode defaults missing/blank to api-key, accepts entra-id case-insensitively, and rejects any other mode; resolveOpenAICompatibleEntraScope trims a custom scope and defaults to DEFAULT_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_ENTRA_SCOPE; providerUsesEntraId is true only for openai-compatible in Entra mode; and getMissingProviderEnvKey returns null for openai-compatible in Entra mode (no static key required) but still requires the key for other providers.
